exceptions.reason: jscpd ships only as a native executable behind a launcher script with no importable API, and the file checks its exit status and report for a missing config, so the process boundary is the thing under test.

These files test the process boundary itself: the bin entry guard under a symlinked launch; the environment a spawned analyzer receives, the force-kill of an analyzer that ignores SIGTERM, and the analyzer scheduler's exit code and cancelled queue under SIGINT and SIGTERM; and that shard aggregation starts with a fresh module graph that loads no development dependency. None of that is observable in-process.

These readers join the report directory nitpicker itself created, the file names the build tools wrote into it, and the source roots the build reported for the project under analysis; none of them comes from user input or from the code under analysis.

Opt-in end-to-end suite that packs the package and runs real npm installs for three dependency layouts (minutes per layout, and removing each installed tree takes long enough to need its own hook timeout); it is skipped unless NITPICKER_INSTALLED_TEST=1.

The shared hook runs ten real analyzers (eslint, prettier, tsc, dependency-cruiser, jscpd and others) side by side over one fixture project, as they run for a user; that takes about eight seconds on an idle four-CPU machine, too close to the ten-second hook limit for a shared CI runner.

The shared hook plans the ESLint config, then runs oxlint with the nitpicker JS plugins over one fixture project, as the eslint-lint analyzer does for a user; each step is a separate process that loads the full rule set, which takes about seven seconds on an idle machine, too close to the ten-second hook limit for a shared CI runner. The tests only read the shared result.

The tests that keep a raised timeout run real nitpicker analyzers (ESLint, TypeScript, Prettier, coverage and Stryker mutation for the full runs) over a copy of a fixture project. Measured on a four-CPU machine while other test suites were running, they take 14 to 52 seconds each, and the full `--all` runs 36 to 79 seconds, so the 30-second default cannot hold them; the tests in these files that take under about ten seconds (a single analyzer or a single edited line) use the default.

The project's tsconfig may still set baseUrl, which TypeScript 6 deprecates and TypeScript 7 removes. The file reads it to rewrite paths into the form tsgolint accepts, so the deprecated option is the input being migrated.
The generated tsconfig must carry an explicit baseUrl: null to unset a baseUrl inherited through extends; undefined is dropped by JSON.stringify and leaves the inherited value in place.
